raw.title: AI Automation Specialist
raw.excerpt: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
raw.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region.

Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp.

Your Career Path in Consulting

Our Consulting team has a clear path, and we hire at every step of it. We place you according to your experience and the impact you have had, and we are explicit about what the next step requires.

  • AI Automation Specialist: Hands-on in the automation itself: you tune agents, run automation sprints and take your first own customers end to end. Typically you bring up to 2 years of experience.

  • Consultant: You own a portfolio of live customers as their run lead, including health, growth and account economics. Typically you bring 3+ years in consulting, process improvement or ERP process ownership.

  • Senior Consultant: Our most complex and sensitive accounts, at executive level, and you coach the Consultants and Specialists around you. Typically you bring several years of leading process change at customers.

  • Next steps: Lead a Consulting team, or become a Client Partner on our strategic accounts.

Moves into Project Management or Customer Success Engineering are open at every level, and many of our people make them.

Your Mission

For a process to run autonomously, four things have to line up: the technology, the process itself, the data behind it, and the people who work with it. That alignment does not happen at go-live. It happens in the months after, and that is where our Consulting team sits.

Our customers go live with a working solution. What they do not have on day one is an organization that operates in an AI-native way. Processes were designed around people checking things. Data was maintained well enough for humans to interpret. Teams know the old workarounds better than the new system. Our job is to lead that transition, from a process that is automated in parts to a process that genuinely runs on its own.

This is also where our AI meets the real world, and the real world is messy. When a customer goes live, our agents start processing their documents: invoices, order confirmations, delivery notes, in dozens of formats from thousands of suppliers, with layouts nobody has seen before. Most of it works immediately. The rest is where we come in.

A concrete example. Our AI learns a customer's business logic from their own history. By reading how they have accounted invoices in the past, blp infers the rules they have been applying and makes them explicit. Sometimes it cannot close the loop on its own, because the same kind of invoice was historically booked in two or three different ways and there is no consistent rule to find. In those cases blp asks. It needs the answer once, and every future case follows it. Making sure that answer arrives, and that it is the right one, is our job. Done well, each of those conversations builds trust and removes a category of manual work permanently.

As an AI Automation Specialist

You are hands-on in the automation itself. You configure and tune the agents so they work for a specific customer, dig into exceptions until you find the actual cause rather than patching the symptom, and run automation sprints: the push after each go-live to the target automation rate, and focused sprints our customers book to take their automation further.

You are in front of customers from early on: running the sessions that explain what a new capability does, taking the open questions our AI raises to the person who can decide them, and chasing down why automation is not landing, whether that is a master data problem, a habit, or a process rule that no longer makes sense. You use data-driven insights to decide which conversations to have with customers and which improvements to prioritize.

You work alongside a Consultant on your accounts and build process and platform depth on real customers from the first month.

Key Responsibilities

Automation and performance

  • Configure and tune agents so they work for a specific customer's documents and processes.

  • Drive and own the push after each go-live, from first live volume to the target automation rate, and deliver the automation sprints our customers book.

  • Resolve the open questions our AI raises about a customer's business logic: take the cases to the customer, get the decision, and make it permanent.

  • Drill into root causes when automation stalls, and tell a master data problem from a process rule from a behavior.

Customer health and growth

  • Own customer health across your portfolio, measured first and foremost by automation rates.

  • Act as run lead and escalation point for your customers once they are live.

  • Challenge process rules that prevent automation, and drive improvements with the department leads who can decide.

  • Enable the customer's core team to resolve issues themselves, and reduce what has to come to us at all.

  • Spot expansion opportunities and bring in Sales, and work alongside the Client Partner on strategic accounts.

Account economics

  • Secure and monitor service consumption against the agreed budgets.

  • Scope automation sprints and additional services, and make sure paid work is billed.

Team and platform

  • Work with our Customer Success Engineers on technical topics, and feed recurring patterns back to Product.

  • As a Consultant, direct the AI Automation Specialists working on your accounts.

What We're Really Looking For

The following key attributes ensure success in this team:

  • Process Excellence – You understand core business processes, P2P and O2C, and you can see why a process is shaped the way it is and what it could look like instead.

  • Client Hands – You bring customers with you. You are strict on the things that matter and flexible on the things that do not.

  • Pattern Recognition – You notice that thirty exceptions are really one problem.

  • Comfort in the Data – You go into the numbers yourself to find where automation is leaking.

  • Ownership – You see a job through, and you take a customer from live to high automation without being told the steps.

  • Growth Mindset – You learn fast, ask when you are stuck, and get better every month.

What You Bring

For the AI Automation Specialist level

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business, Economics, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field. Strong career changers are equally welcome.

  • Up to 2 years of professional experience. Internships, working student roles or a first analytical job count.

  • Structured, analytical way of working and solid command of Excel or equivalent.

At every level

  • Confident in front of customers, from operational teams to their leadership.

  • Fluent in German and English, spoken and written.

  • Bonus points for experience with ERP systems, accounts payable or order management processes, data skills such as SQL or Python, or AI-driven SaaS.

Benefits

  • High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path.

  • Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises.

  • Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily.

  • Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option program.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Technology exposure – be at the forefront of AI and enjoy continuous learning opportunities.

  • Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

Learn more about blp and our values at .

About Ema

Ema is building the world’s leading Agentic AI platform to transform enterprise productivity. We enable organizations to delegate repetitive tasks to Ema, the Universal AI Employee, delivering 10x gains in workforce efficiency, across functions. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production — we ship real systems that run real business processes at scale.

About the role

Ema is building the Universal AI Employee, and we expect our own operations to run the same way. We're hiring our first dedicated IT Engineer to own corporate IT end to end: identity, devices, SaaS and compliance across 200+ devices in the US, UK, Canada and India.

This isn't a help desk role. You'll run IT while systematically automating it, using agentic tooling to remove manual work rather than absorb it. Success is measured by how little of the job is still manual after a year, and how good every employee's IT experience is.


What you’ll do

  • Treat every recurring task as an automation candidate, building workflows with Python, Bash, APIs, Okta Workflows and AI coding tools

  • Own the joiner, mover and leaver lifecycle with People Ops via Rippling → Okta → SCIM, moving it from tickets to policy-driven automation, including access reviews

  • Administer Okta, Google Workspace, Slack and Atlassian; configure SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM and MFA across all apps

  • Manage the Mac fleet in Kandji: enrollment, automated OS patching, encryption baselines and continuous drift detection

  • Maintain SaaS inventory and usage programmatically, and reclaim unused licenses automatically

  • Generate evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001 and AI governance frameworks continuously, as a byproduct of automated operations

  • Maintain runbooks, a knowledge base and an integration registry; provide Tier 1/2 support within defined SLAs

  • Be the go-to for Finance and HR on tool access, licensing, renewals and billing

What success looks like

  • 90 days: Onboarding and offboarding are automated end to end; SaaS inventory is live and license reclamation is running

raw.description:
Wanted: Colonist DevOps Engineer

Working Hours: We work asynchronously and value outcomes over hours

Location: Fully Remote

Compensation: Paid in USD. Negotiable based on experience and location

About Colonist

We're building the biggest digital board game platform on the internet. Players start 250k games every day. Last year: 60M games, 3,037 years of play. We're a fully remote, asynchronous team spread across multiple continents, focused on crafting extremely polished digital board games that people truly love.

About The Role

Most apps scale by splitting users apart. We can't. Players share one live game state. Every lag spike is felt mid-game. One viral video can 10x our traffic overnight. Your job: absorb 50k CCU without dropping a single game.

You will own the infrastructure behind every game session: clusters, deploys, databases, the edge, and the path from merge to production. You will make our infra knowledge shared, so no system depends on one person.

What You'll Do

  • Own the stack behind every game: game, matchmaking and lobby servers on Kubernetes

  • Manage cluster and cloud resources as code in Terraform

  • Scale servers up and down with live traffic. Pay for players, not idle machines

  • Ship updates often, without kicking players out of live games

  • Keep terabytes of game data and replays fast and cheap. PostgreSQL, Redis, NATS under real load

  • Defend the edge from bots and attacks. Cloudflare, rate limiting, Turnstile, R2.

  • Own observability across Sentry and New Relic. Consolidate monitoring and close the gaps

  • Document everything: systems, decisions, runbooks, so infrastructure knowledge lives in the team

  • Build self-service paths so other engineers use infrastructure confidently.

  • When something breaks, thousands notice in seconds. Find the root cause. Make it never recur

Requirements

  • You love hard technical problems. Scale, latency and cost excite you

  • You have senior-level experience in DevOps

  • You have run Kubernetes in production: rollouts, autoscaling, networking, load balancers, and debugging a bad deploy

  • You run infra lean. You optimize before adding hardware

  • You document as you go. Runbooks and decisions are natural outputs of your work.

  • You are comfortable with Linux, Docker, and a CI system you did not build

  • You have operated PostgreSQL and Redis under real traffic: slow queries, connection limits, and schema migrations without downtime

  • You have run a message broker in production; we use NATS, but equivalent experience transfers

  • You have put Cloudflare, or a similar edge, in front of a public service

  • You can debug a live incident across app logs, metrics, the database, and the edge

  • AI-forward mindset. We see AI fluency as a real multiplier

  • Deeply independent. You learn a system from its code, configs and monitoring.

  • Strong written communication. You explain complex systems clearly in async settings, to technical and non-technical audiences alike

  • Collaborative by default. You share context proactively, help other engineers understand infrastructure, and never operate as a silo

Nice to Have

  • Experience structuring documentation for AI consumption: machine-readable runbooks, structured architecture notes, agent-readable formats

  • Experience building self-service infrastructure paths for other engineers: golden paths, templates, or internal tooling

  • Security depth beyond the basics: threat modelling, access control, audit practices, governance guardrails

  • You've run real-time or multiplayer systems where shared state matters.

  • Previous experience as a solo or near-solo infrastructure engineer at a small company

Our Values at Colonist

We strongly adhere to these values in our team - if these resonate, then you'll love working here!

Dependability

We're self-driven players who deliver without needing supervision. When we commit to something, we make it happen.

Ownership

We take full responsibility and go beyond our roles to improve Colonist.

Clear Communication

In our remote environment, written communication is key. We're direct, structured, and always keep our team in the loop.

Efficient Execution

We move fast and focus on impact. Instead of getting stuck on perfect solutions, we find practical ways forward and get things done.

Continuous Learning

We're curious problem solvers who love a challenge. We constantly seek new ideas, embrace feedback, and aren't afraid to change our minds when we're wrong.

Why Colonist

  • Your work ships to 3,6M+ yearly active players

  • We have hard problems, most engineers only read about: live shared state, viral spikes, lean scale

  • Async culture; deep work, no performative meetings

  • Unlimited vacation, yearly team offsite, full work equipment

  • Budget to experiment with any AI tool you want

  • Access to all company metrics and internal discussions

raw.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region.

Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp.

Your Mission

You get customers live. Hands on, end to end, and fast.

As a Project Manager, most of your implementations are not multi-year global programs. They are for companies that want blp running in their finance or supply chain organization within weeks, and who want somebody who knows what they are doing to take them through it. You are that person. You run the kick-off, work with them on scope and process, configure blp, coordinate the integration, take them through testing, and get them across the line at go-live.

You work in three modes, and many of our Project Managers move between them:

  • Guided onboarding for our commercial customers: you run configuration days for several customers at once, guide them while they configure, and answer the questions that come up.

  • Leading yourself on enterprise customers: you own the project end to end, including the sponsor meetings.

  • Alongside a Senior Project Manager on our largest programs, where you take a country, an entity or a workstream and own it.

Your Career Path in Project Management

This is the path most of our delivery leadership came through, and we hire at every step of it. We place you according to your experience and the size of the programs you have delivered, and we are explicit about what the next step requires.

  • Project Manager: You get customers live end to end, several in parallel: guided onboarding for commercial customers, leading enterprise projects yourself, or a workstream on our largest programs. Typically you bring 2+ years in consulting, implementation or project management.

  • Senior Project Manager: You make large, global transformations happen: multiple ERPs, entities and countries, the steering committee, and a blp team on each engagement. Typically you bring 5+ years delivering complex, multi-country programs.

  • Next steps: Lead a delivery team, or move into Consulting and from there towards our Client Partner role on strategic accounts.

Moves into Consulting or Customer Success Engineering are open at every level, and many of our people make them.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run implementations end to end: kick-off, scope, planning, configuration, testing and go-live.

  • Manage several customers in parallel at different stages, and keep every one of them on date.

  • Work with customers on their processes, and flag early where a process assumption will not hold.

  • Coordinate the specialists on your projects: Integrations Engineers, Technical Project Managers and AI Automation Specialists.

  • Own scope actively. Recognize a change request for what it is and handle it deliberately.

  • Keep the project inside its budget, and raise it early when the effort is drifting.

  • Hand over cleanly at go-live to our Consultants and support organization.

In addition, as a Senior Project Manager

  • Own the delivery outcome of global programs from kick-off to the last go-live: plan, scope, dependencies and date.

  • Drive the first go-live relentlessly, then run wave planning across ERPs, entities and countries.

  • Run the steering committee and own the decisions that come out of it.

  • Write and execute the recovery plan when a program is off track.

  • Lead the blp team on each engagement and coach the Project Managers working on your programs.

What We're Really Looking For

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

  • Scope Discipline – You notice when a project is quietly growing, and you raise it rather than absorbing it.

  • Ownership & Autonomy – You take initiative, move things forward, and deliver end to end without being chased.

  • Escalation Judgment – You escalate early, to the right person, with a proposal rather than a problem.

  • Client Confidence – You are comfortable running a meeting with a customer's finance or IT lead in it.

  • Four-Language Fluency – Technology, process, data and people. You speak each well enough to spot where a roadblock really sits.

  • Structured Under Pressure – When a project goes sideways you get sharper and more organized, not louder.

What You Bring

For the Project Manager level

  • Master's degree in Business, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

  • 2+ years of experience in consulting, technical implementation, process automation, or project management.

  • The ability to run several projects at once without losing control of any of them.

  • Strong analytical and communication skills. You can translate a business need into something a technical team can act on.

  • Fluent in German and English, spoken and written.

  • Bonus points for ERP implementation experience, finance or supply chain processes, or AI-driven SaaS.

Benefits

  • High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path.

  • Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises.

  • Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily.

  • Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option program.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Technology exposure – be at the forefront of AI and enjoy continuous learning opportunities.

  • Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

Learn more about blp and our values at .

The Kind of Builder We Want 

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (Immuware) - Remote, US
description: Propelus® simplifies workforce compliance management across healthcare.

raw.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (Immuware) - Remote, US
raw.excerpt: Propelus® simplifies workforce compliance management across healthcare.
raw.description:
Propelus® simplifies workforce compliance management across healthcare. Our innovative technology and strategic partnerships empower millions of professionals, their employers, and regulators to work together, creating a connected and efficient healthcare ecosystem.

As a trusted leader for over 20 years, Propelus has focused on bringing more good into the lives of the people and organizations serving healthcare. We deliver seamless compliance solutions to millions. We leverage market-leading technology and essential data to simplify complex operations, reduce risk, and champion a safer, healthier, and happier workforce.

About the Role:

Immuware's customers, including Employee Health nurses; occupational health managers; and compliance professionals, work in one of the most requirement-heavy environments in healthcare IT. Regulations shift. Organizational structures change. New workflows emerge. Each of these changes often means hands-on work is needed inside their Immuware environment.

The Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) exists to meet that need. You are both technically driven and a proactive, friendly, and compelling person.

You will be embedded in the post-sales customer experience, you are not an account management, not executing billable project work, and not break-fix support.

You show up on customer calls, quickly understand the technical needs of a health-system nurse manager and what they are trying to accomplish, and provide the polished product quickly, ensuring a positive experience.

What You'll Do:

As our Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) you will be the proactive technical resolution of customer problems end to end:

From meticulously understanding the clients needs and proactively building those solutions, you ultimately serve as the bridge between customer needs and internal product and engineering teams.

You're measured on customer outcomes, not on activity.
This role partners closely with our Customer Success Managers, who own the overall customer relationship, strategy, and commercial outcomes.


Technical Solutioning & Building

  • Lead regular (often weekly) technical working sessions with customers to address actively evolving needs driven by regulatory changes, organizational shifts, and workflow updates.

  • Identify, configure, script, and write code to solve customer needs: workflow setup, rule-building, field configuration, user and role management, reporting, data corrections, integrations, and small platform changes.

  • Translate complex Employee Health requirements (OSHA compliance, state-specific immunization mandates, system credentialing workflows, and the like) into solutions that actually work for our clients, in the Immuware platform.

  • Question their requirements and requests: Serving as the techncial expert, professionally challenge requests that don't serve the customer's real goal, and choose the simplest solution that solves the underlying problem to improve efficiency operationally.

  • Thoroughly document your solution designs in Notion, while updating live items in Jira, to ensure they are clear, well-scoped bug reports and feature requests that are repeatable and transferable to enable engineering efficiency.

  • Generalize your work: Turn one-off fixes into reusable templates, decision trees, or product improvements so the next customer benefits.

  • Triage net-new module or record-type additions that need a formal Letter of Work (LOW) and/or an ARR change (expansion) to CSMs and Professional Services.

Customer Partnership

  • Serve as the technical counterpart to CSMs on customer calls: CSMs handle the relationship; you independently handle "how do we make it work."

  • Navigate internal client change: working alongside the CSMs, lead deeper, in-depth customer education beyond basic platform navigation, run workflow specific walkthroughs, and re-train as staff turnover and organizational change creates knowledge gaps.

  • Serve as the technical expert: build trusted-advisor relationships with power users and technical contacts at customer organizations.

    • Proactively identify configuration gaps or risks before they turn into escalations, and execute solutions to maintain the strong client relationship

  • Detail Oriented: Stay aware of each assigned customer's various environment, history, and upcoming needs.

    • Confidently identify and navigate between "I can fix this," "this needs a support ticket," and "this needs a product change."

You'll Thrive in This Role If You

  • Are energized by customer calls and like solving problems live, not async.

  • Can read a healthcare compliance requirement and immediately start thinking about how to model and build it in a SaaS platform.

  • Have a builder's mindset: you're systematic, you test your own work, you write code when it's the right tool, and you don't leave a solution half-done.

  • Can switch comfortably between explaining something to an IT admin, a head nurse, a customer executive, and your own engineering team.

  • Are naturally organized. You manage several customers with different environments and needs at once.

  • Get frustrated by workarounds and push internally for real solutions.

We'd Like It If You Had:

  • 5+ years in a technical, customer-facing role(solutions engineer, implementation consultant, technical account manager, or forward deployed engineer)

    • handling client resolutions, both live (virtually) and post meeting action items, and know how to navigate delays while staying calm under pressure and maintaining the clients trust.

  • 4-5 years navigating Azure, JavaScript, and Typescript with a strong background in SQL and Azure SQL database management.

  • 2-3+ experience operating in Notion and Jira

  • Proficiency in C#, and comfort reading a codebase, debugging, and writing scripts or small features, and track record of building on SaaS platforms, not just toggling settings: creating non-trivial workflows, rules, forms, reports, integrations, or role and permission structures.

  • Drive and ownership: You are comfortable and familiar with identifying the crux of large, enterprise customers' problems and outline additional potential issues as well. Then you own the solution outcome, driving these problems to resolution on your own instead of handing them off.

  • Strong written and verbal communication: You're credible with a customer's executives and technical staff and with internal product and engineering teams, and comfortable leading technical working sessions with non-technical stakeholders.

  • You handle delays, bugs, and scope pushback while keeping the customer's trust.

  • Structured problem-solving: You have experience scoping an issue for large, enterprise clients, find the root cause, and propose a solution in a live setting and navigate how to implement these solutions to our smaller accounts.

  • Comfort working without a playbook: you'll hit novel problems regularly and need to adapt as policies and regulations change.

  • Written reporting experience: familiarity writing clear, well-scoped bug reports and feature requests that engineering teams can act on.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in healthcare IT, Employee Health, or occupational health.

  • Familiarity with immunization tracking, credentialing workflows, or OSHA and state health reporting requirements.

  • Familiarity with APIs and integrations, plus comfort with SQL or scripting for data investigation and fixes.

  • Prior use of Immuware or similar platforms (Tyto Care, Equifax I-9, or Symplr)

What This Role Is Not:

  • Not account ownership. CSMs own renewals, expansion, and the executive relationship. The FDE supports those relationships through technical excellence.

  • Not billable Professional Services. PS handles formal implementation projects with SOWs. The FDE handles ongoing, post-go-live technical needs as part of the customer's subscription.

  • Not the L1/L2 support queue. The support team owns routine bug triage. This FDE will do deeper scoping and fixes, ensuring a clean handoff. It does not replace the support workflow.

What Success Looks Like:

30 days: Support an active deal

Within the first month, you will have built context on the healthcare customers motion, platform capabilities, common implementation needs, and regulated data considerations. They are supporting an active customer engagement with guidance.

60 days: Lead a solo engagement

After two months, you are now independently leading a scoped customer sync, having built trust with customers technical teams, and delivering against customer requirements and timelines.

90 days: Own multiple, concurrent engagements

At three months in, you are now independently managing multiple healthcare customer engagements, contributing reusable playbooks and tooling, and surfacing product feedback that helps convert bespoke implementation patterns into scalable capabilities.

If your experience is close but doesn't fulfill all requirements, please apply. We're building the best team in healthcare and are focused on hiring individuals with unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences to support us in doing good, what’s human, and making a difference.

Benefits and Perks for Propelus Employees

US Employees:

  • Health Insurance: We cover up to 100% of the premium for employee medical insurance. Plans for spouses and children are made affordable through Propelus’ generous contribution

    • Employees can choose from HSA, FSA, and traditional insurance options for medical, dental, and vision coverage for themselves and dependents.

    • Dental and Vision plans, both including an option with 100% of the premium covered for employees

  • Generous PTO:

    • Accrual: (full-time US): 0–4 yrs 20 days | 5–9 yrs 25 days. | 10+ yrs 30 days per year (accrues quarterly: Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, Oct 1; and is available immediately).

    • US-based teams observe 14 paid holidays each year

    • Floating Holiday: One floating holiday is yours to request on any day of your choice. This is separate from your PTO.

    • Birthday Holiday: Your birthday deserves celebrating! You get 1 paid day off during your birth month, separate from your PTO.

    • Volunteer Time Off: 16 hours available to you, that allow you to make an impact on causes that are meaningful to you.

    • Additional leave options: to support you in embracing life centricity

    • State & local leave laws

      • Where state or local leave laws provide additional protections, Propelus will comply with whichever regulation is more favorable to the employee.

  • 401K with company matching, as well as financial planning education and resources.

  • Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA): We support personal well-being by offering an annual lifestyle spending account that you can use for what matters most to you—whether it’s a gym membership, a meditation app, WFH equipment, or fresh produce delivered to your door. Think of it as a bonus for the expenses and experiences you value most.

  • Employee Assistance Programs: provides 24/7/365 support by phone and online — family clinical counseling, legal & financial services, plus child and elder care referrals.

  • Carrot Fertility & Hormonal Support: Inclusive hormonal health, fertility, and family-building benefits with funds toward eligible care.

  • Beyond Med: A licensed discount plan organization (DPO) giving you access to elective care like acupuncture, dermatology, fertility, GLP-1, and more — at discounted rates.

  • Spot Pet Insurance: A financial safety net for your furry family. Get reimbursed for emergencies, lab fees, behavior, x-rays, surgeries, cancer, and more.

LATAM (Costa Rica and Colombia) Employees:

  • Your health is our top priority! We cover 100% of employee health insurance premiums. Our plans include national and international coverage, so you're protected no matter where you are.

  • Propelus Flex Club: Our flexible benefits platform gives you monthly points to redeem on what you need most. Plus, you'll get access to exclusive discounts just for being part of our team. (Details are country specific)

  • Generous PTO:

    • National Holidays (Colombia): 18 days

    • National Holidays (Costa Rica): 12 days

    • Birthday Holiday: Your birthday deserves celebrating! You get 1 paid day off during your birth month, separate from your PTO.

    • Volunteer Time Off: 16 hours available to you, that allow you to make an impact on causes that are meaningful to you.

    • We've got you covered with a life insurance policy, paid 100% by the company. You can also add your beneficiaries at an exclusive, discounted rate.

    • Carrot Fertility & Hormonal Support: Inclusive hormonal health, fertility, and family-building benefits with funds toward eligible care.

Benefits and Perks for ALL Propelus employees include but are not limited to:

A remote first company, global and distributed, with two office locations for those nearby who want a change of scenery.

  • A remote first company, global and distributed, with two US office locations for those nearby who want a change of scenery, and one in CO and CR.

  • Employees celebrating their 10 and 20 year work anniversary are eligible to take a trip sponsored by Propelus within one year of their 10th and 20th anniversary date.

  • Awarded one of BuiltIn's 2025 Best Places to Work and honored as a Silver Stevie® Award Winner in the 2025 Stevie Awards For Great Employers.

  • Professional development allowance to help you grow in the ways that mean the most to you.

  • Check us out for yourself at our careers page or our Propelus culture Instagram accounts.

Typical Interview Process:

  • Interview #1: Brief intro screen with our People Ops team

  • Interview #2: Introduction with the Hiring Manager

  • Interview #3: Team Panel

  • Interview #4: Alignment interview with Senior Leadership

If you don’t move forward to the next round, we’ll make sure you know as soon as possible.

Tips for applicants: Focus on your application. At Propelus, everyone has an equal opportunity based on their merit. Reaching out to the team or providing referrals will not change your chances.

We work remotely and communicate asynchronously, so writing is a key skill at Propelus. Please answer the application questions with your own thoughtful responses. Replies like "See resume" or N/A won't lead to an interview. Have some fun with it, we actually read these!

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at Propelus. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Candidates from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

Full-time positions are scheduled to work 40 hours per week, M-F unless required otherwise by projects. Part-time positions are scheduled to work a maximum of 30 hours per week. Equipment, benefits, and perks are not provided to part-time or temporary employees.

Compensation Range: $120K - $140K

raw.title: Technical Writer
raw.excerpt: vCluster Labs is looking for a Technical Writer to join our documentation team.
raw.description:
vCluster Labs is looking for a Technical Writer to join our documentation team. You'll write and maintain conceptual, how-to, and reference documentation across the vCluster Platform, working from design docs alongside engineers and standing up tenant clusters yourself to verify every procedure before it's published. Our docs serve a wide audience, from prospects evaluating vCluster to platform engineers. This is a hands-on role. You'll need to actually run the software, not just read about it, to write docs that hold up.

As a Technical Writer, your role will include:

  • Documentation: Write and maintain conceptual, how-to, and reference documentation for vCluster, vCluster Platform, vMetal, and related tenant-isolation concepts.

  • Verification: Stand up tenant clusters yourself to verify procedures, capture screenshots, and confirm CLI output before publishing.

  • Collaboration: Work from projects, tickets, and design docs. Collaborate with engineers to fill documentation gaps surfaced by support and sales.

  • Information architecture: Contribute to product information architecture, naming conventions, hierarchy, and concept organization across the docs site.

  • Review and editing: Review and edit for consistency with our terminology and style guide.

This role could be a fit for you if you bring:

  • Kubernetes fundamentals: Working knowledge of Kubernetes fundamentals (pods, namespaces, control planes) and comfort using a terminal to run commands like kubectl and helm. You should have enough to understand the docs you're writing or reviewing, not necessarily enough to design a system yet.

  • Technical writing: 2+ years of technical writing experience. You have demonstrated prior experience of strong technical writing.

  • Workflows: Familiar with ticket trackers (GitHub Issues, Jira, Linear or similar), async collaboration with engineers on a global team, automated style/lint enforcement (such as Vale), and versioned documentation workflows.

  • AI usage: You're comfortable and excited to use AI in your writing workflow, from drafting docs off tickets and design docs to using an AI coding assistant to verify a procedure works before writing it up to automating work with skills and agents.

Bonus points for:

  • Prior experience with container orchestration, platform engineering, or infrastructure tooling

  • Experience with tooling like Docusaurus, MDX, or similar

  • Start-Up Grit: Experience working in a high-growth environment. You are comfortable with ambiguity and eager to make an impact.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive Salary: We offer a competitive compensation package, including equity.

  • Premium Insurance: Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country).

  • Flexible Working Schedule: You have a doctor’s appointment or need to head to the supermarket to get groceries at 2pm? We won’t have an issue with that. To us, results matter more than clocking in and out at the same time every day.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

CourseCareers is an online education platform that helps people launch new careers without a college degree or prior experience.

Our students are career changers looking for realistic, entry-level roles — and coaching helps bridge the gap between coursework and landing the job.

We’re looking for a part-time Construction Estimating Career Coach to support students through live workshops and optional 1:1 coaching.

This is not a traditional employment role and not a guaranteed-income position. It’s a flexible, paid opportunity best suited for construction estimating professionals who enjoy mentoring, teaching, and helping others break into the field — with upside if students choose to work with you.

How This Role Actually Works

  • You host a live, one-hour workshop (seminar-style) for students

  • You are paid $50 per workshop, plus any private coaching business you acquire

  • You may receive exclusive coaching opportunities based on performance and engagement

  • Workshops are used to provide value, answer questions, and showcase your expertise

  • If students choose to book you for 1:1 coaching, you keep the coaching revenue

  • You set your own availability and working hours

There is no requirement to convert students — workshops are paid regardless — but conversion is where the upside comes from.

Responsibilities

  • Host a live, one-hour workshop on a monthly basis

  • Answer student questions related to construction estimating and the job search

  • Share real-world insight into what entry-level estimating roles actually look like

  • Explain how estimating works in real construction environments (GCs, subs, specialty trades)

  • Discuss common tools, workflows, and expectations

  • Provide optional 1:1 coaching to students who request it

What We’re Looking For

  • 3+ years of professional construction estimating experience

  • Experience estimating for GCs, subcontractors, or specialty trades (e.g. concrete, electrical, mechanical, roofing, etc.)

  • Familiarity with estimating tools such as Excel, PlanSwift, Bluebeam, ProEst, or similar software

  • Strong understanding of entry-level roles like Estimating Assistant, Junior Estimator, or Project Coordinator

  • Interest in mentoring and helping career changers

  • Strong communication and teaching ability

  • Availability at least three evenings per week, ideally Tuesday–Thursday

  • Self-starter mindset — comfortable leading workshops independently

Ideal Fit

This role is a great fit if you:

  • Enjoy teaching and mentoring

  • Want flexible, side income

  • Like the idea of being paid to teach — with optional upside

  • Don’t need guaranteed hours or full-time income

Compensation

  • $50 per one-hour workshop (One per month guaranteed)

  • Unlimited upside from 1:1 coaching sessions you convert

  • No caps, no quotas, no minimums

raw.description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia. As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges.

We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved.

What you'll be doing

  • Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.

  • Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.

  • Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.

  • Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.

  • Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.

  • Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.

  • Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.

What you'll need

  • Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

  • Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

  • Domain— experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).

  • AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.

  • Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

Outcomes

  • Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

  • Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

  • Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

  • AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

  • Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

  • Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

Location

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Hong Kong. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Hong Kong.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

About the Role

You'll be the third designer on a fast-moving, remote-first team building identity and onboarding infrastructure for businesses globally. Design is central to what differentiates this product, and you'll shape how complex financial and compliance workflows become intuitive, conversion-focused experiences. This is a high-ownership role where your work spans system foundations to end-to-end user journeys.

What You'll Do

  • Build and maintain a modular design system that powers both live product implementations and Figma prototypes.

  • Design complex onboarding flows that adapt to multi-step, modular customer needs.

  • Apply a conversion-focused mindset by measuring, testing, and refining every step of the user experience.

  • Prototype quickly and systematically, iterating on ideas based on customer feedback and data.

  • Collaborate closely with front-end and back-end engineers to ensure designs translate seamlessly into production.

  • Help shape design culture and establish standards that enable the team to scale.

What We're Looking For

  • 4 to 6+ years designing complex products or workflows, ideally in B2B SaaS, enterprise tools, fintech, or compliance environments.

  • Demonstrated experience building and maintaining design systems with modular components that work across Figma and live implementations.

  • Experience designing for compliance, fintech, or identity and KYC workflows.

  • Strong systems thinking: you design scalable, interconnected solutions rather than isolated screens.

  • Analytical rigor: you treat user interactions and journeys as testable, optimizable hypotheses and make data-informed decisions.

  • Hands-on collaboration with front-end and back-end engineering teams to bring designs to production.

  • Proficiency with Figma for design system creation, prototyping, and component management.

  • A habit of documenting design decisions, trade-offs, and learnings to keep teams aligned.

  • Comfort navigating complexity and ambiguity while moving quickly.

  • Experience establishing design standards and culture within growing teams is a plus.

Location

This role is fully remote, open to candidates based in EU timezones. The primary location is France, though candidates across the EU are welcome. Visa sponsorship is not available.

raw.excerpt: About UsCurvion is a high performance RevOps & sales augmentation agency that installs and deploys enterprise-grade, AI-driven revenue engines and selling systems for our clients.
raw.description:
About Us

Curvion is a high performance RevOps & sales augmentation agency that installs and deploys enterprise-grade, AI-driven revenue engines and selling systems for our clients. Think of a lead generation based marketing agency…. But focused on sales! We design and install complete sales systems from sales processes and GTM strategy to CRM setup all the way to fully outsourced sales engagements. Then we enhance those systems with AI enabled tools and battle tested playbooks, and finally, we provide highly trained sales talent to help our clients execute so their revenue engine runs faster, scales efficiently, and performs consistently. In short, we build and power modern, AI-driven sales systems that help companies grow with clarity and control.

Position Overview: RevOps Solutions Specialist

The RevOps Solutions Specialist sits at the intersection of sales, RevOps, HubSpot, and solution design.

You’ll work directly in the sales process to understand prospective clients' current sales operations, identify gaps and opportunities, and translate those findings into a clear RevOps solution.

You need to know HubSpot extremely well, but this role is much bigger than HubSpot.

You’ll help determine what systems, workflows, automations, integrations, processes, and operational infrastructure a client actually needs. From there, you’ll help scope the project, define deliverables, build the SOW, and develop pricing.

In other words, you’re the person who helps turn:

"Here's our sales problem."

into:

"Here's what Curvion should build, here's how we'll build it, and here's what it will cost."

You’ll work closely with the sales and delivery teams throughout the deal cycle, helping ensure that what we sell is technically sound, properly scoped, commercially viable, and deliverable.

This is an agency role. You’ll work across multiple prospective and active client environments, each with different sales processes, systems, and business requirements. Experience working in a client-services environment is critical.

Ideal background: HubSpot Solutions Partner, HubSpot agency, RevOps agency, CRM consultancy, or similar technology/implementation agency.

You SHOULD apply to this role if:

  • You have agency, consultancy, or client-services experience

  • You’ve preferably worked for a HubSpot Solutions Partner, HubSpot agency, RevOps agency, CRM consultancy, or similar organization

  • You’ve worked with multiple clients and HubSpot environments

  • You know HubSpot extremely well and have built real-world systems

  • You understand how sales teams actually operate, not just how CRMs work

  • You’ve participated in discovery, solution design, scoping, or technical sales conversations

  • You can look at a client's sales operation and quickly identify gaps and opportunities

  • You can translate a business problem into a technical and operational solution

  • You have experience creating SOWs, proposals, scopes, implementation plans, or project estimates

  • You understand how to evaluate project complexity, effort, resources, and pricing

  • You’re comfortable working alongside sales throughout the deal cycle

  • You can explain technical concepts to executives and non-technical decision makers without making their eyes glaze over

  • You can balance what the client wants, what they actually need, and what Curvion can realistically deliver

  • You enjoy being the bridge between sales and delivery

You SHOULD NOT apply to this role if:

  • Your HubSpot experience has only been internal to one company

  • You have no agency, consulting, or client-services experience

  • You’ve never worked across multiple client environments

  • You know HubSpot but don't understand sales or RevOps

  • You don't enjoy discovery conversations or client interaction

  • You've never had to scope a project or define deliverables

  • You aren't comfortable thinking about project effort and pricing

  • You need someone else to tell you what solution to recommend

  • You prefer staying completely behind the scenes

  • You’re uncomfortable being accountable for what gets sold and scoped

Core Outcomes

  • Prospective client needs are translated into clear RevOps solutions

  • Sales opportunities are properly scoped before they reach implementation

  • SOWs accurately define the solution, deliverables, and expectations

  • Pricing reflects the actual complexity and requirements of the engagement

  • Proposed solutions are technically sound and operationally realistic

  • Sales and delivery remain aligned throughout the deal cycle

  • Clients understand what Curvion is recommending and why

  • New projects enter implementation with clear scope and minimal ambiguity

General Expected Duties

  • Participate in sales discovery calls to understand prospective clients' sales processes, systems, challenges, and goals

  • Audit and evaluate prospective clients' HubSpot environments and broader RevOps infrastructure

  • Identify gaps across CRM architecture, sales processes, automation, reporting, integrations, and operational workflows

  • Translate discovery findings into recommended RevOps solutions

  • Design solution architecture and implementation plans

  • Determine project scope, deliverables, dependencies, and requirements

  • Build SOWs, scopes, proposals, and other sales enablement materials

  • Partner with sales leadership to develop project pricing based on scope and complexity

  • Collaborate with delivery teams to validate technical feasibility and implementation requirements

  • Support sales conversations by answering technical and RevOps questions

  • Communicate complex technical solutions in clear, business-focused language

  • Maintain alignment between what is sold and what can actually be delivered

  • Support the handoff from closed deal to implementation

  • Continuously improve Curvion's RevOps solution frameworks, scoping methodology, and pricing models

Compensation & Logistics

Job Type: Full-time, W-2
OTE: $72,000 - $100,000 annually
Additional Compensation: Bonus opportunities
Schedule: Monday-Friday, 9:00 AM-6:00 PM
Location: Remote

Compensation Range: $72K - $100K

raw.excerpt: About AbridgeAbridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare.
raw.description:
About Abridge

Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients.

Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems.

We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Social Media Marketer to own how Abridge grows across social. This is a role for someone who treats social as a performance channel with a funnel behind it: someone who can build an audience from a standing start, run a real experiment cadence, and connect audience growth to outcomes further down the funnel like email capture, content consumption, event registration, pipeline influence, and recruiting.

Abridge is an AI company building in healthcare, and we have the substance to build a meaningful public presence: a product that clinicians use and love, a team of practicing physicians and AI researchers, and a CEO who is himself a practicing cardiologist. Two conversations we should be central to, the AI conversation and the healthcare conversation, are happening every day on social without us in them. What we need is someone who can close that gap deliberately, with a plan, a stack, and a number they're accountable to.

Writing matters in this role. You'll be publishing in the brand voice and in the voices of our executives and clinicians, and the work has to be native and genuinely good. But the hard requirement here is growth: we're looking for a growth operator who writes well, not a writer who also reads dashboards. You'll have editorial and creative partners for the craft, and you'll be the one deciding what to test, what to scale, what to kill, and what any of it did for the business.

This role reports into Growth and partners closely with Creative, Comms, Product Marketing, Customer Marketing, Events, and Recruiting. You'll own social strategy, channel prioritization, distribution, experimentation, and measurement end to end.

What You'll Do

  • Own audience growth as a number. Set and hit targets for follower growth, reach, and engaged audience by platform, and own the framework that connects social activity to ToFu, MoFu, and BoFu outcomes. Be able to say what a month of work produced and what you'd do differently next month.

  • Build and own the measurement layer. Define the metrics that matter, instrument the tracking (UTM discipline, analytics, self-reported attribution, event and campaign tagging), and report to marketing leadership on a regular cadence. Bring insights back that change what we make.

  • Run a continuous experiment program. Maintain a live backlog of hypotheses across hooks, formats, cadence, first frames and thumbnails, posting time, cross-posting, and audience targeting. Design tests that can actually be read, and be disciplined about killing what doesn't work.

  • Decide which platforms we play on and how. Own LinkedIn and X as our primary channels, and make the call on where else we should be investing across Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, TikTok, etc. Each one has a different audience, algorithm, and reason to exist for us.

  • Build the growth stack outside the native platforms. Stand up and operate the tooling that makes growth repeatable: publishing and scheduling, audience research and enrichment, listening and monitoring, link tagging, competitive and creator tracking, reporting. Automate the parts that should be automated, with clear judgment about where third-party tooling crosses a line we don't want to cross as a healthcare company.

  • Use paid amplification where organic hits a ceiling. Partner with Growth to put budget behind what's working, run retargeting off social audiences, and understand the interplay between organic reach and paid distribution.

  • Build an employee and executive amplification program that runs as a system. Identify the right internal voices among our clinicians, researchers, executives, and subject-matter experts, and build the operating model that keeps them posting: content supply, drafting support, approval flow, tooling, and measurable reach. Success here is a program that works without you writing every post.

  • Publish at a high standard and at real volume. Write, edit, ship, and iterate across posts, threads, carousels, comments, executive content, short-form video, and emerging formats. Know when something needs polish and when speed and native execution matter more.

  • Identify the stories worth distributing. Proactively find what's worth posting across the company (product launches, customer impact, research, clinicians, events, cultural moments, the people building Abridge) and bring a strong point of view on the angle and the channel.

  • Partner with Creative to get assets made. Brief designers, writers, videographers, and agencies with clear strategic and creative context. Contribute to ideation, give useful feedback, and treat creative partners as collaborators.

  • Build community. Reply with intention, surface customer and community voices, participate where our audiences actually are, and create real-time moments around launches and flagship events.

  • Use AI as a force multiplier. Incorporate AI throughout your workflow, from audience research and ideation to drafting, editing, repurposing, analysis, and reporting. Experiment with new tools and workflows, and have a considered view on where AI makes the work better and where it doesn't.

  • Partner across marketing and the company. Work alongside Growth, Product Marketing, Customer Marketing, and Events. Bring a distribution and audience perspective into planning early, and turn company priorities into social opportunities.

What You'll Bring

  • Five to eight years in social media marketing or growth marketing, with direct hands-on ownership of social as a growth channel.

  • A demonstrated track record of growing an audience, with real numbers attached. You can walk through what the account looked like when you started, where it got to, and specifically what drove it.

  • Fluency with the funnel. You've been held accountable to metrics beyond engagement, and you can explain how you connected social activity to downstream outcomes like email signups, registrations, demo requests, or pipeline, including where the attribution was imperfect and how you worked around it.

  • Analytics and attribution chops. You're comfortable in platform analytics and in tools like GA4 or Amplitude, you're rigorous about tagging and tracking, and you can build a report that leadership actually uses.

  • Hands-on fluency across multiple platforms, including LinkedIn and X, plus real working knowledge of at least a couple of others (e.g., Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, and TikTok). You understand the cultural, algorithmic, and creative differences between them and can create natively for each.

  • Experience with the tooling layer around social. You've built or automated workflows for publishing, audience research, listening, enrichment, or reporting, and you have a point of view on which tools are worth it and which create more risk than value.

  • Experience running paid social, even at modest budget, and an understanding of how paid and organic compound.

  • Strong writing and editorial judgment. You can find the hook, write an opening line that earns attention, develop an idea clearly, and edit your own work. You don't need to be the best writer on the marketing team, but you need to be good enough that nothing waits on someone else to make it publishable.

  • Experience building executive, employee, or subject-matter-expert voices. You've helped people become credible public voices and can speak specifically to what made the program work and how you kept it running.

  • An AI-native working style. You use AI every day, have considered opinions about where it strengthens the work and where it weakens it, and actively experiment with new tools and workflows.

  • Experience inside a high-growth technology or AI company, where priorities move quickly and you're often creating structure where none exists.

  • Exceptional execution. You're comfortable moving fast, making decisions with incomplete information, and shipping consistently.

  • Strong cross-functional influence. You can bring people together around a point of view and move work forward without formal authority.

  • A proactive, low-ego mindset. You're curious, generous with your expertise, and motivated by work that compounds.

Bonus Points

  • You've grown a personal presence on X, LinkedIn, YouTube, or TikTok to a meaningful following.

  • You've grown an audience in a regulated or specialized industry, where credibility is built slowly and mistakes are expensive.

  • You've built communities: Slack groups, subreddits, newsletters, events.

  • Experience in healthcare, health tech, or selling to clinical audiences.

Working at Abridge

This position requires a commitment to a hybrid work model, with the expectation of working from our San Francisco or NYC office a minimum of three days per week. Relocation assistance is available for candidates who are willing to move to San Francisco or NYC.

Why Work at Abridge?

At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month.

Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business.

Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients.

We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you.

How we take care of Abridgers:

  • Generous Time Off: 14 paid holidays, flexible PTO for salaried employees, and accrued time off for hourly employees

  • Comprehensive Health Plans: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for all full-time employees and their families.

  • Generous HSA Contribution: If you choose a High Deductible Health Plan, Abridge makes monthly contributions to your HSA.

  • Paid Parental Leave: Generous paid parental leave for all full-time employees.

  • Family Forming Benefits: Resources and financial support to help you build your family.

  • 401(k) Matching: Contribution matching to help invest in your future.

  • Personal Device Allowance: Tax free funds for personal device usage.

  • Pre-tax Benefits: Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Commuter Benefits.

  • Lifestyle Wallet: Monthly contributions for fitness, professional development, coworking, and more.

  • Mental Health Support: Dedicated access to therapy and coaching to help you reach your goals.

  • Sabbatical Leave: Paid Sabbatical Leave after 5 years of employment.

  • Compensation and Equity: Competitive compensation and equity grants for full time employees.

  • ... and much more!

Equal Opportunity Employer

Abridge is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants equally without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability.

We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the interview process. Once you submit your application, we'll follow up with details on how to request an accommodation for interviewing, completing any assessments, or otherwise participating in the selection process.

Staying safe - Protect yourself from recruitment fraud

We are aware of individuals and entities fraudulently representing themselves as Abridge recruiters and/or hiring managers. Abridge will never ask for financial information or payment, or for personal information such as bank account number or social security number during the job application or interview process. Any emails from the Abridge recruiting team will come from an @abridge.com email address. You can learn more about how to protect yourself from these types of fraud by referring to this article. Please exercise caution and cease communications if something feels suspicious about your interactions.

Compensation Range: $155K - $175K
